title: A Little Bowl for Garden Animals
paras: In 1978, Rosa had a small garden behind her house. Summers were hot, and she [[often|often]] saw thirsty animals there. One morning, a [[baby|baby]] [[rabbit|rabbit]] sat near her empty bucket. Rosa brought some [[water|water]] outside in a soup bowl. The little animal drank from [[it|it]]. This gave Rosa an idea. Her garden needed a place where small animals could drink.

The next day, she bought an old clay bowl for one [[dollar|dollar]]. She put [[half|half]] of the water from her bucket into the bowl. Then she added a flat stone. Deep water could be [[dangerous|dangerous]] for small animals. The stone gave them a place to stand. With a [[knife|knife]], she cut some string and tied a small sign to her gate.

The sign said, “A drink for our garden friends.” Her neighbour, Kenji, liked the idea. Rosa gave him another bowl. “[[thanks|Thanks]]!” he said. Soon, five gardens on their street had animal drinking bowls. Every morning, people washed the bowls and filled them again. Years later, Rosa's bowl broke. Kenji brought her a new one, and the small garden practice went on.
zh: 1978年，罗莎的屋后有一个小花园。夏天很热，她经常在那里看到口渴的动物。一天早上，一只幼兔坐在她的空水桶旁。罗莎用汤碗盛了些水，端到外面。小兔子喝了碗里的水。这让罗莎有了一个主意。她的花园需要一个能让小动物喝水的地方。
第二天，她花一元钱买了一个旧陶盆。她把桶里一半的水倒进盆里，然后放入一块扁平的石头。深水对小动物来说可能很危险。这块石头让它们有地方站脚。她用刀切下一段绳子，把一块小牌子绑在自家院门上。
牌子上写着：“给花园里的朋友们喝点水。”她的邻居健二喜欢这个主意。罗莎送给他另一个盆。“谢谢！”他说。很快，他们街上有五户人家的花园都放了供动物喝水的盆。每天早上，人们都会把盆洗净，再装上水。多年后，罗莎的盆碎了。健二给她送来了一个新的，这个花园里的小习惯就这样延续了下去。

q.s: The baby rabbit came to Rosa's garden every day.
q.why: 只提到一天早上的幼兔，未说它每天都来。

q.s: Rosa put half the water from her bucket into the clay bowl.
q.why: 第二段明确说她倒入了桶里一半的水。

q.s: Kenji gave Rosa a new bowl before her old bowl broke.
q.why: 旧盆先碎了，健二才送来新盆。
